## Themes

humanlayer_skills design-control-loop, analysed for the first time (41 traits), ruled under the owner's rulings of 2026-11-22 and 2026-11-24 (bead cr-p3em.6): adopted, adapted, as the control-loop skill. Kept: the control vocabulary, the grounded interview part by part, the written design, the golden pattern, one home per rule, the assembled prompt and the steering file, the one-open-pull-request bound, by-hand runs before any schedule. Changed: an allowlisted agent in place of broad permissions, a loop instructions file in place of an actuator skill, fix or skip with no ignore entry, a local timer on request in place of a CI workflow, one real run in place of a push-trigger dry run, a lock that skips in place of cancelling. Rejected: the /iterate comment channel and its stage-all path, the agent committing and pushing, a manual bypass of the bound, parallel pull requests, broad permissions, the illustrative example.

Suggested: control-loop · purpose match: control-loop · flag: none
Purpose: Upstream designs a scheduled control loop with a person (sensor, controller, actuator) that opens one small pull request per run through a CI workflow. Ours: the control-loop skill, built from it by the owner's rulings, which designs the same loop and runs it locally first, with its state in Beads, an allowlisted agent and a gated commit by the run script.
Reason: Overlap, placement and purpose agree on control-loop.

### Blind extraction

1. control-vocabulary: Frame the loop in control terms (set point, sensor, controller, actuator, disturbances, the result fed back into the next run, a person on the loop) and walk the person through them before designing anything. (SKILL.md:12-22; R/control-loop-taxonomy.md:1-19, 30-51)
2. read-repo-first: Before asking setup questions, read the CI configuration, package manager files, validation scripts, existing skills and agent loops and the analysis tooling, done when the package manager, install and validation commands, CI platform and loop conventions can be named. (SKILL.md:26, 43-56)
3. design-interview: Design the loop with the person as an interview, component by component, proposing options grounded in what the repository has and surfacing trade-offs rather than mandating a choice, recording decisions as they go, from a fixed list of design questions. (SKILL.md:10, 27, 58-62; R/control-loop-taxonomy.md:3-5, 65-75)
4. set-point-scope: Fix the set point as an invariant, a threshold or a direction, and pin the scope: the paths the loop may change and the paths it may only read. (SKILL.md:64; R/control-loop-taxonomy.md:11; R/prompt-template.md:5-9)
5. sensor-choice: Choose the sensor from the repository's existing tooling (lint, structural search, tests, type checker, telemetry, a script or an agent), weighing stability, cost, repeatability and whether it can be silently disabled, so the controller can act on it repeatably. (SKILL.md:66; R/control-loop-taxonomy.md:13; R/example-control-loop.md:17)
6. controller-increment: The controller picks the next increment, sized to stay low-risk and reviewable (which target, how many, in what order), deterministic or agentic, with each run capped by a count of findings, files or packages. (SKILL.md:68; R/control-loop-taxonomy.md:15, 62)
7. controller-tuning: Start the controller simple and tune it over time from the loop's output and the person's corrections. (SKILL.md:68, 132; R/control-loop-taxonomy.md:15)
8. fused-components: Let sensor, controller and actuator fuse where the design fuses them (a ranking tool, one agent that picks and changes) and collapse their steps, never inventing separation. (SKILL.md:115; R/control-loop-taxonomy.md:21-28; R/example-control-loop.md:21-23, 45)
9. agent-pick: Pick the headless coding agent, its secret and its non-interactive command from per-agent templates. (SKILL.md:71; R/agent-runner-templates.md:1-14)
10. golden-patterns: Before automating, find in the code what a good change looks like, confirm with the person which existing patterns to follow, and encode them in the actuator's instructions. (SKILL.md:72, 86)
11. validation-bar: Agree the validation commands that must pass before the agent commits, proposed from what the repository already runs. (SKILL.md:73; R/skill-template.md:39-43; R/prompt-template.md:20-25, 38)
12. dampener-offer: Name the disturbances acting outside the loop and offer, as optional, a dampener: a check on pull requests that compares the sensor's output with a baseline and surfaces newly introduced deviations, advisory first and blocking once trusted. (SKILL.md:75; R/control-loop-taxonomy.md:19, 60; R/example-control-loop.md:37-39)
13. written-design: Write the agreed design down (set point, sensor, controller, actuator, disturbances and dampener) before building, so the person can correct it cheaply. (SKILL.md:29, 77)
14. actuator-skill: Write a repository-local skill holding the actuator's judgement: ordered steps with checkable completion criteria, long templates in references, the golden patterns, a review checklist, and a frontmatter name equal to its folder. (SKILL.md:36, 79-93; R/skill-template.md; R/example-skill.md)
15. single-source: Keep each rule in one place, never repeated across the actuator skill, the prompt and the memory file. (SKILL.md:87)
16. response-template: Give the agent a response template for its final message, which becomes the pull request body: summary counts first, grouped by resolution, risk levels shown prominently, manual verification steps for riskier changes. (SKILL.md:88; R/response-template.md:1-103; R/skill-template.md:45-49)
17. fix-ignore-skip: Give each target three honest outcomes: fix it, ignore it by adding it to the tool's ignore configuration with a reason, or skip it for a person. (R/example-control-loop.md:27; R/response-template.md:12-35)
18. local-first: Make the sensor and controller version-controlled scripts, then run the sensor, the controller on real sensor output and the actuator through its headless command by hand, each standalone, before any CI exists. (SKILL.md:28, 95-107; R/control-loop-taxonomy.md:53-55; R/agent-runner-templates.md:7-14)
19. ci-workflow: Wire the loop into a scheduled CI workflow (one CI system by default) as discrete sensor, controller and actuator steps, then commit and open a pull request whose body is the agent's final message. (SKILL.md:37, 109-121; R/workflow-template.yml:1-20, 173-253)
20. cadence-choice: Choose the cadence (daily, weekdays, weekly, monthly, manual only or a custom schedule) by the task's risk and review burden. (SKILL.md:117; R/workflow-template.yml:15-16)
21. prompt-assembly: Assemble the actuator's prompt from a fixed structure (context, scope, instructions, validation commands, rules, output format), then the controller's selected work, then the memory file. (SKILL.md:118-119; R/prompt-template.md:1-58; R/workflow-template.yml:192-213)
22. no-asking: Tell the unattended agent never to stop and ask for feedback or approval. (R/prompt-template.md:32)
23. memory-file: Keep a version-controlled memory file of durable guidance (scope exclusions, known false positives, reviewer feedback that should change selections, never one-off instructions or run logs), loaded into the actuator after the controller on every run. (SKILL.md:38, 127-129; R/memory-template.md:1-7; R/control-loop-taxonomy.md:63; R/workflow-template.yml:200-212)
24. iterate-comments: Let a maintainer comment /iterate on a loop pull request: authorized commenters only, routed by a hidden marker in the body to the workflow that opened it, which loads the pull request and memory, updates the pull request and distils durable guidance into the memory file. (SKILL.md:130-134; R/workflow-template.yml:3-9, 18, 33-41, 66-84, 138-170, 254-265; R/agent-iteration.ts)
25. open-pr-bound: Bound work in progress at one open pull request per loop: label each loop pull request (with a title and branch prefix) and have a scheduled run no-op when one with the label is open. (SKILL.md:136-145; R/control-loop-taxonomy.md:59; R/workflow-template.yml:55-62, 251-253)
26. manual-bypass: Let a manual dispatch bypass the open pull request bound. (SKILL.md:142; R/workflow-template.yml:65-69)
27. validate-workflow: Parse the workflow file and confirm every path the skill, workflow and memory file name exists or is created by the task. (SKILL.md:151, 157)
28. push-dry-run: Dry-run by adding a temporary push trigger, watching the run, removing the trigger, and reviewing the pull request it opens. (SKILL.md:153, 157)
29. iterate-faster: Once tuned and consistent, raise throughput: a more frequent schedule, a wider batch, several sense-control-actuate cycles per run, or several runs each giving one pull request to a different teammate. (SKILL.md:155)
30. broad-permissions: Run the agent with a permission mode that bypasses its permission checks (or a full-access sandbox), on trusted isolated runners. (R/agent-runner-templates.md:3, 31, 70-71, 96)
31. spend-guard: Cap the agent's turns or spend where the repository needs it. (R/agent-runner-templates.md:37)
32. response-extraction: Extract the agent's final message from its output into the pull request body file, per agent, falling back to the raw output or a placeholder when extraction fails. (R/agent-runner-templates.md:5, 39-49, 77, 99-111, 135-147, 155-157; R/workflow-template.yml:222-227)
33. no-commit-no-pr: Open no pull request when the agent made no commit. (R/workflow-template.yml:237-240)
34. scope-gate: Restrict the actuator to safe directories, excluding generated, vendored or high-risk code unless explicitly selected. (R/control-loop-taxonomy.md:61)
35. cancel-in-progress: One run per loop at a time: a new run cancels the one in progress. (R/workflow-template.yml:26-28)
36. stage-all: The iteration path stages every change (git add -A), commits and pushes to the pull request branch. (R/workflow-template.yml:256-263)
37. agent-commits: The agent itself validates, commits and pushes its change. (R/prompt-template.md:17-18, 34-40)
38. worked-example: Show one fully worked loop as an illustration of the shape to copy, never a template of its specifics. (SKILL.md:22; R/example-control-loop.md:1-3, 54-57; R/control-loop-taxonomy.md:5)
39. phase-criteria: End every phase on a checkable completion criterion. (SKILL.md:56, 77, 93, 107, 121, 134, 145, 157)
40. keep-agent-output: Keep the agent's raw output as a run artifact for debugging. (R/agent-runner-templates.md:155; R/workflow-template.yml:267-272)
